title: Max Flow Value
prompt:
**Bài toán.** Line 1: n m s t; then m lines u v c. Print the
maximum flow from s to t.

**Constraints:** 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 2000; 1 ≤ c ≤ 10^9. Small enough for
Edmonds–Karp; cancellation via residual arcs is required.

tests.name: classic diamond
tests.hint: Two parallel 2-routes plus the crossing edge: max flow 4 — the crossing edge is never needed.

tests.name: cancellation required
tests.hint: A greedy first-path push saturates 1->2 the wrong way; residual back-edges fix it. Answer 2.

tests.name: bottleneck chain
disconnected sink
augmenting path required
tests.hint: Greedy DFS takes s→b→a→t first, saturating a→t; only the residual arc can reroute to s→a→t + s→b→t = 2. Without residual arcs the answer stays 1.

tests.name: two disjoint paths, one stolen middle
tests.hint: Max flow 2: 1→2→3→4→7 and 1→5→6→7 are edge-disjoint. A no-residual DFS crosses onto the second route via 3→6 and saturates 6→7, stranding both: it reports 1. Only the residual arc can cancel 3→6's unit and reroute it through 3→4.
